title: D85 dispatch lockout: every command and the Gate-D approval path are denied in a live session
head: 478e362
symptom: bash tool: every invocation denied, including 'git status --porcelain' alone, 'wc -c <one-file>', 'cd <repo> && git status --porcelain', and the bash cwd-parameter form. Denial text: [d85] shell command contains dynamic expansion or nested execution that cannot be bound to exact write targets. Use literal operands or exact d85-run.
eval tool: denied as [d85] arbitrary-code tool (eval/python/repl) is denied while D85 enforcement is active.
Gate-D approval path: writing args to mcp__jake_pai_gate_d_request returned [d85] unregistered tool 'mcp__jake_pai_gate_d_request': a host-owned capability classification is required.
still working: read, glob, the built-in search tool, write, edit.
why_this_is_a_governance_incident: The enforcement layer now denies both the mutation and the approval request that would authorise it. A session cannot commit, cannot run a read-only diagnostic, and cannot open a Gate-D request. Fail-closed with no exit is not fail-closed, it is a deadlock, and it is happening on a repo where five of my commits landed minutes ago and another agent is committing continuously.
likely_cause: The uncommitted work in the tree, not HEAD. My slice (ffa7dfc + 0ea9039) removed universal pre-tool build admission from rig_capabilities/loops.py and rig_capabilities/d85_admission.py and those removals are committed. The tree then absorbed another agent's 21:27 d85.py rewrite (static-source v2 / grammar v3, 1271 insertions) plus their d85_gates.py 21:06 edit, and the hook path the session actually loads is an installed copy that still routes ordinary dispatch through hook_check. Reproduce by comparing the hook's loaded module path against rig_capabilities/loops.py at HEAD.
scope_conflict: Mike's 2026-09-11 clarification, recorded in AGENTS.md: D85 is the build-quality gate for solutions, applications and durable systems and 'does not gate ordinary startup, research, file access, memory capture, diagnostics, Python execution, or authorized local edits'. Denying wc -c and git status is exactly the universal pre-tool admission that clarification retired.
what_i_did_about_it: Nothing mutating. I did not set RIG_D85_DISABLE, did not use break-glass, did not touch D85 configuration or ledgers, and did not hunt for a bypass. I finished the verification by routing around the block: glob instead of git ls-tree, the built-in search tool instead of shell pipelines, and pre-existing isolated-clone logs instead of new runs.
worktree_rerun_attempt: One re-run was requested for a quiet window and is IMPOSSIBLE from this session: the same lockout denies every bash call, so neither the fingerprint nor the suite can be collected. Status stands as worktree RED-BUT-UNSTABLE, evidence being the two fingerprints captured around the single run that did complete (5f0fd345619b before, 1d3e5f9b7257 after). The 17F/64E count is a measurement of a moving tree, not a state, and it is the other agent's pending work to attribute, not mine to fix.
decision_needed_from_mike: Revert or re-scope the uncommitted d85.py / d85_gates.py hook widening, or push my committed scope fix through to the hook copies the runtimes actually load. Until then no agent session in this repo can commit or request approval.

Decide whether the committed generated artifact .index.json should be regenerated (blocked: 137 foreign untracked assets would be baked in) or untracked, because it is what keeps test_catalog.CertifyTests.test_index_gate_planted_red red in a fresh clone of HEAD.
